priorStories.headline: Haiti sends 18 assassination suspects to US
priorStories.body:
Eighteen suspects in the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse were flown from Haiti to the United States to face trial, according to U.S. and Haitian officials.

U.S. prosecutors have indicted 30 people in the case. Haiti’s justice minister said proceedings there had produced no trial after five years of delays.

priorStories.headline: Ukraine launches vast drone attack across Russia
priorStories.body:
Ukrainian forces launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia overnight, according to officials cited by the Associated Press. Russian authorities reported three deaths in the Moscow region and damage to an oil refinery and residential buildings.

Ukraine said it targeted oil and logistics facilities. The casualty, interception and damage reports come from the countries fighting the war and could not be independently reconciled.

candidates.summary: Russia's Central Election Commission said United Russia won 57.83% of the party-list vote after more than 95% of ballots were counted in the parliamentary election. The preliminary result would give the ruling party 355 of the State Duma's 450 seats, preserving its constitutional majority. The election was conducted under tight political controls, with voting also held in Russian-controlled areas of Ukraine that Kyiv and Western governments reject as illegally occupied.
candidates.title: United Russia retains constitutional majority in preliminary count

candidates.summary: China's Foreign Ministry announced that President Xi Jinping will make a state visit to the United States from September 23 through September 25 at President Donald Trump's invitation. The ministry did not provide further itinerary details in its initial announcement.
candidates.title: China confirms Xi state visit to United States

candidates.summary: Typhoon Dujuan brought heavy rain and strong winds to eastern Japan as it approached the Pacific coast. At least 275 flights were canceled, more than 4,000 households in Chiba Prefecture lost power, some railway services were suspended and authorities warned of flooding and landslides. Japan's weather agency said rainfall through Tuesday could exceed the monthly September average in some areas.
candidates.title: Typhoon Dujuan disrupts travel and power in eastern Japan

candidates.summary: The Gates Foundation announced that it is convening a coalition of 60 organizations, including Anthropic, Google and the OpenAI Foundation, to develop more representative language data for artificial intelligence. The coalition aims to make AI tools more accessible to more than 3 billion people over five years, though details including its governance remain under development.
candidates.title: Gates Foundation convenes coalition for underrepresented AI languages

candidates.summary: Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee said persistent supply shocks, including oil-price increases and tariffs, may require higher interest rates that push employment below its target to return inflation to 2%. His remarks described a policy trade-off and did not announce a Federal Reserve decision.
candidates.title: Goolsbee says inflation fight may require economic pain

candidates.summary: U.N. Special Rapporteur Mariana Katzarova presented a report to the Human Rights Council describing Russian surveillance, intimidation and reprisals against critics abroad as a systematic state strategy. The report, based on about 400 documented cases, said recorded incidents increased after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Russia's Geneva mission did not immediately respond to Reuters and Moscow has previously denied allegations of hostile actions abroad.
candidates.title: UN expert reports expanded Russian repression abroad

sources.name: Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights

candidates.summary: An unidentified projectile struck a tanker entering the Strait of Hormuz, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center. Two crew members sustained minor injuries, while the vessel continued toward its next port under its own power. No environmental impact was reported initially.
candidates.title: Projectile strikes tanker entering Strait of Hormuz

candidates.summary: The International Organization for Migration reported that renewed fighting in Yemen had displaced 129,438 people across seven provinces. The agency said 11,352 people were displaced during the three days beginning September 18, with many families having already fled their homes more than once.
candidates.title: Yemen fighting displaces nearly 130,000 people, IOM says
